clue.text: French peace-making organization in brawl

parts.note: ACAS, the UK Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, settles industrial disputes

explanation.surface: A French peacekeeping body somehow finds itself caught up in a punch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is a British body that mediates in workplace disputes; 'in' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy quarrel or scuffle is a brawl, the same rowdy fight.

clue.text: It might strike one as relatively modern weapon

explanation.surface: A newer gun could hit someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A repeater is a watch or clock that chimes the hour again when pressed, and also a rifle that fires several shots without reloading.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiming watch can strike the hour, and a magazine rifle was a nineteenth-century firearm.

clue.text: Act as beater in hunt — it's held up

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for hunt

parts.note: to hunt is to chase

indicators.note: held up, in a down clue, means the word it's is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A beater on a shoot is delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'held up' means read upwards; 'in' puts the result inside the hunt word. The definition plays on beating as punishment, not driving game.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish physically is to beat, so the word means act as a beater of wrongdoers.

clue.text: The poet Burns, drunk with wine

indicators.note: drunk shows the letters of Burns and wine reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Robert Burns has had too much wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles BURNS plus WINE. Burns is a poet too, but here only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon Charles Swinburne was a Victorian English poet.

clue.text: Book tough defender

parts.note: tough means hard
a back is a defending player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A tough footballer in defence is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-covered edition is a kind of book, as opposed to a paperback.

clue.text: Training for the upper classes?

parts.note: reads like schooling for toffs, but means education at a more advanced level, at university

explanation.surface: Schooling designed for the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: University and college study comes above school level, so it is advanced training.

clue.text: Caught in 12 perhaps, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in puts the cricket letter inside the rearranged word
perhaps suggests the letters of that answer could be arranged differently

parts.note: 12 refers to the answer of 12 across, DETAIL
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Something caught in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DETAIL (12 across) into DIALET, and C goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional form of a language is a particular way of talking.

clue.text: Inform about article to make assessment

indicators.note: about means the word for inform goes around the article

parts.note: to apprise is to inform
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is told about an item so they can judge it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside APPRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or value something is to make an assessment of it.

clue.text: Writer includes this play to make Peking learn

indicators.note: to make says the letters of Peking learn are rearranged, the pen's letters included

parts.note: this is the result of the pen wrapping the play, PE before and N after; the run inside it comes from that wrapping, a coincidence of construction rather than a separate hidden-word device
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An author fits a play into the curriculum so Beijing will study it.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the play inside PEN (PE...N) and you get PEKING LEARN; equivalently, those letters are the answer plus PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of an old king and his daughters is a play.

clue.text: Conversation piece initially taken by Viking chief

indicators.note: taken by says that letter is held inside the Viking chief

parts.note: a sea-king was a Norse pirate chief

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of the word piece is wanted

explanation.surface: A Viking leader seizes a topic for chat.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea-king is a Viking chieftain; P, the first letter of 'piece', goes inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking together, as in being on speaking terms, is conversation.

clue.text: Take place, perhaps, in 6

explanation.surface: An event occurs, perhaps, in some local speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is DIALECT: in northern English dialect 'happen' means perhaps ('happen it'll rain').
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to take place, and in Yorkshire or Lancashire speech the word also means maybe.

clue.text: Soldiers' food is not insipid

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, are soldiers; TA'S is their possessive
table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: Army rations are claimed to have some flavour after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be savoured has flavour, so it is not bland or insipid.

clue.text: Particular military detachment

explanation.surface: A fussy point about a small group of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is an individual item or point, and a small party of troops assigned to a task is also so called.

clue.text: Officer worsted soldier, perhaps

parts.note: serge is a worsted woollen cloth
a soldier is one caste of ant

explanation.surface: An officer has beaten an ordinary soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worsted' looks like a verb meaning defeated, but it is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned rank in army or police is an officer.

clue.text: With proper fencing, one's good and close

definitions.text: With proper fencing, one's good and close

parts.words: With proper fencing, one's good and close
parts.note: the person next door, close by, stays friendly

explanation.surface: With a decent fence, the person next door is friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Frost's poem 'Mending Wall' says 'Good fences make good neighbors'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living nearby is close, and the proverb promises good relations with them.

clue.text: Liberal? Not bound to be so

explanation.surface: A politician of the Liberal party claims independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous or unrestricted is liberal, and being unbound or at liberty is the other sense.

clue.text: Scapegoats descend on hospital

parts.note: to descend is to fall
Guy's is a famous London teaching hospital

explanation.surface: Those who take the blame come down on a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's Hospital is in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Those set up to take the blame for others are scapegoats.

clue.text: Steps said to secure my pardon

explanation.surface: Someone apologises by stepping aside.
explanation.walkthrough: An excuse-me is a dance in which a partner may be claimed by someone cutting in.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance steps named for the cut-in dance, and the polite phrase spoken to ask forgiveness.

clue.text: Put up tower

explanation.surface: Someone builds a tall structure.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or build up, and to loom high over something, are both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Turn right several turns later

indicators.note: turns shows the letters of several being twisted into new order

explanation.surface: Turn right, and later turn again several times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'later' places the anagram (signalled by 'turns') after R, the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A change of direction or fortune is a turn.

clue.text: West Indian insect and tailless lizard

parts.note: an ant is an insect

indicators.note: tailless means the lizard loses its final letter

parts.note: an iguana is a lizard

explanation.surface: Caribbean creatures: an insect and a lizard without a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the last A from IGUANA.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Antigua, in the Caribbean, is a West Indian.

clue.text: What do vicars do? Epistle's included in new duties

indicators.note: included in says the epistle abbreviation sits inside the rearranged letters
new tells us the letters of duties are made afresh in another order

parts.note: EP is an abbreviation for epistle

explanation.surface: Clergy find a letter from the apostles has been added to their workload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the anagram and 'included in' the insertion. A vicar was originally a stand-in for the rector, so the question is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar originally acted on behalf of a rector, so vicars stand in or substitute for others.

clue.text: Assumed gear could be lined up precisely

explanation.surface: Someone put on kit and fell into neat line.
explanation.definitionFit: Having put on clothes, and troops aligned in exact ranks on parade, are both senses.

clue.text: Source of praise for Scottish comedian

explanation.surface: Praise comes from a comic north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Harry Lauder was a famous Scottish music-hall comedian and singer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who lauds gives praise, and Harry Lauder was the celebrated Scots entertainer.

clue.text: Fit and unusually lithe at 100

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of lithe at appear in a different order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Someone is remarkably supple and healthy at the age of a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges LITHE AT into ATHLETI, then C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sporty and in good physical shape is being fit.

clue.text: Anxious in mind as a monarch when lying?

explanation.surface: A king lies awake fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Henry IV says 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Worried and ill at ease is anxious, and the quotation says a crowned head lies restless.

clue.text: Clears up clubs abroad

parts.note: irons are golf clubs
abroad can mean out of doors, out

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are cleaned up while overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve difficulties is to clear them up or smooth them away.

clue.text: Descend a bit to leave office

explanation.surface: A leader comes down a little and resigns.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down a single stair is descending a bit, and resigning a post is the idiom for leaving office.

clue.text: Decision made in drawing the line?

explanation.surface: Someone decides where to set the limits.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's verdict is a decision, and marking straight lines with a ruler is the second sense.
